info.title: Invinite API
info.description:
Invinite financial data API. Each endpoint has a base credit cost: `x-credits` is the base cost; responses add 1 credit per started 1,000 rows beyond the first 1,000; `X-Credits-Charged` reports the final debit and `X-Credits-Included-Remaining` what is left of the plan's included credits. `GET /v1/account/usage` returns your account's usage by day, endpoint family and key (it costs no credits). SEC filing search has a 100-credit base cost.

## Webhooks

Accounts on LITE and above subscribe with `POST /v1/earnings-calls/webhooks` to the `earnings_call.*` lifecycle events (filtered by CIK); see `x-webhooks` for each `data` object. What a subscription may hold depends on the plan (a create / update beyond it is refused with the plan's limit; `ping` needs no subscription — the test route and the disabled notice send it to any subscription):

| Plan | Webhooks | Events | CIKs per webhook | Keywords per webhook |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| FREE | 0 | — | — | — |
| LITE | 5 | `.scheduled`, `.rescheduled`, `.started`, `.ended`, `.transcript_ready`, `.assets_ready` | ≤ 10 | — |
| STANDARD | 15 | LITE + `.transcript_provisional`, `.transcript_corrected`, `.documents_updated` | ≤ 25 | — |
| PRO / ENTERPRISE | 50 | STANDARD + `.guidance_flash`, `.keyword_hit` | ≤ 100 | ≤ 20 (on ≤ 10 webhooks) |

Every delivery is a `POST` with `Content-Type: application/json`, `X-Invinite-Event`, `X-Invinite-Delivery` and `X-Invinite-Signature: t=<unix seconds>,v1=<hex>` where `v1` = HMAC-SHA256(secret, `<t>.<raw body>`); during a secret rotation the header carries one `v1` per valid secret. Reject a signature older than 5 minutes. Any 2xx within 10 s acknowledges; redirects are not followed. A failed delivery is retried after 1 min, 5 min, 30 min, 2 h, 6 h, 12 h, 24 h (8 attempts in all, the same delivery id each time). A subscription is disabled after 8 consecutive dead-lettered deliveries (a final `ping` with `notice: subscription_disabled` is sent). Deliveries are at-least-once and unordered: dedupe on the delivery id, order by `created_at`.

## Licensing

| Tier | display | redistribute | rag | train | audio | resell |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FREE | ✓ | – | – | – | – | – |
| LITE | ✓ | – | – | – | – | – |
| STANDARD | ✓ | – | ✓ | – | – | – |
| PRO | ✓ | ✓ | ✓ | – | ✓ | – |

Invinite data may be shown and, from PRO, redistributed inside the licensee's own product with attribution ("Source: Invinite" on screen or in the API response that carries it). It may never be resold, relicensed, white-labelled or offered as a data feed as the licensee's own data, at any tier, under any contract.

Policy version: 2026-10-draft. Draft — pending counsel sign-off.

Audio files are forensically watermarked per customer. Audio is served through signed URLs, is subject to per-company takedown and may not be re-hosted; every delivered file carries a per-account forensic watermark: a copy found elsewhere is traced to the account that received it.

SEC data: Figures and filings originate from SEC EDGAR; the standardisation, mapping and derived metrics are Invinite's.

Every `/v1/*` data operation carries `x-license`, the minimum use right its data ships with; `GET /status/licensing` serves the same matrix per route, rendered at [data.invinite.com/docs/licensing](https://data.invinite.com/docs/licensing). `/v1/account/usage` serves no licensed data and carries none.

## Status

[`/status`](/status) reports whether each product family works (a status and its uptime over 7, 30 and 90 days); [`/status/licensing`](/status/licensing) serves the licensing matrix per route. The status routes need no API key and are cached for 5 minutes. The public status page is [status.data.invinite.com](https://status.data.invinite.com): a snapshot of `/status` every 15 minutes plus an external reachability probe of the API.

Uptime is the share of requests answered without a server error, measured by the API per product family; a window with too little traffic to judge shows no figure. Status reflects the last 24 hours.

Product families: Company, Financials, SEC Filings, Insider Trades, Institutional Ownership, IPOs, Market, Metadata, Earnings Calls, WebSocket, Account.

WebSocketNewFilingEvent.description: Broadcast when a new SEC filing finishes processing

WebSocketPingEvent.description: Server heartbeat payload sent when protocol-level ping is unavailable

WebSocketSubscribeEarningsCall.description: Client frame: subscribe to the live transcript of one earnings call, by event_id or by cik (the call that is live or starts within ±2 h), or with scope: all_live (no event_id / cik) to every call being captured live — keyword hits only, never segments, one subscription slot. Requires the PRO plan.

event_id.description: Event id from the earnings-calls REST routes

scope.description: all_live = every live call (keywords required, error keywords_required without); then no event_id / cik

since_seq.description: Last final seq the client holds; finals after it are replayed before live delivery (-1 = from the first final)

partials.description: Also receive partial (not yet final) segments

prices.description: Also receive price_tick frames of the call's stock (≤ 1 per second while the call is live). Per-call only: with scope: all_live the subscribe is refused (bad_message). GET /v1/earnings-calls/live says live_prices: true when ticks flow

keywords.description: Keyword alerts: a keyword_hit frame for every FINAL segment that contains one (whole words, case-insensitive, multi-word allowed). Held for this subscription only

keyword_match.description: exact = whole-word match of your spelling (buyback never matches buybacks); stem = also s / es / ed / ing / 's per word (tariff matches tariffs)

speaker_roles.description: Only hits spoken by one of these roles (from the provisional live speaker names; a hit whose speaker is still unnamed passes)

min_rank.description: all_live only: calls of companies ranked ≤ min_rank by market cap

events.description: all_live only: what reaches the subscription (default keyword_hit; add guidance_flash to receive the flashes of every live call)

WebSocketSubscribedEvent.description: A subscription is active. A per-call subscription carries the call (event_id … state); a scope: all_live subscription carries scope, keywords and live_calls instead

current_seq.description: Highest final seq seen so far; null before the first final (seqs start at 0)

keywords.description: all_live only: the keywords as held

live_calls.description: all_live only: calls being captured live that the subscription follows right now

WebSocketKeywordHitEvent.description: A subscribed keyword occurred in a FINAL segment (layer live; partials are never evaluated) or, once per subscription at transcript_ready, in the final transcript (layer final; a final hit within ± 5 s of a live hit of the same keyword is not repeated). The only call-level frame of a scope: all_live subscription besides guidance_flash

keyword.description: The subscriber's own spelling of the keyword

seq.description: The live final's seq; null on the final layer

start_ms.description: Offset from the start of the recording

end_ms.description: null on the final layer when the cleaned text has no end timing

text.description: The segment (live) or turn (final), at most 500 chars

context_before.description: The previous final / turn of the call (≤ 300 chars); a final is often half a sentence

speaker_name.description: From the live speaker-name snapshot (null while unnamed) or the final transcript

speaker_role.description: executive | ir_host | analyst | operator; null while unnamed

layer.description: live = a live final; final = the final transcript at transcript_ready (once per subscription)

latency_ms.description: live only: relay time inside the API process minus the segment's own end time (excludes the client's network); null when the call's clock is unknown

WebSocketGuidanceFlashEvent.description: A forward-looking guidance number extracted from the live transcript seconds after it was spoken (one frame per metric / period; a restatement repeats it with a higher revision). Sent to every subscription of the call and to all_live subscriptions whose events include guidance_flash. Provisional: the structured guidance of /v1/earnings-calls/extractions replaces it after the call

seq.description: The final that triggered the extraction

revision.description: 1 for the first flash of a metric / period; higher when the numbers were restated

low.description: Lower bound of the range (absolute units)

point.description: A point value when no range was given

source_sentence.description: The verbatim sentence the numbers come from

start_ms.description: Offset of the sentence from the start of the recording

WebSocketPriceTickEvent.description: One second of the call's stock price while the call is live (≤ 1 per second, only seconds with a trade — hold the last value and draw a missing second as a gap; pre-market and after-hours bars are sparse). Sent only to per-call subscriptions with prices: true. Temporal coincidence, not attribution of cause. The minute rows of /v1/earnings-calls/price-attribution are the backlog for a late join

at.description: Start of the one-second bar (ISO 8601 UTC)

call_ms.description: The bar start on the transcript clock (the start_ms of transcript_segment frames); null before the call's clock is known — then chart it on wall time (at)

price.description: Last price of the second, shown while the call is live

cumulative_volume.description: Shares traded so far today; null when unknown

reference_price.description: The call's reference: the last trade before the call start (for a late join, the previous close)

return_bps.description: Return since reference_price, basis points; null without a reference

day_return_bps.description: Return since prev_close, basis points; null without it

source.description: stream = the real-time per-second bar; snapshot = the polled last trade while the stream is down (open = high = low = price)

WebSocketWarningEvent.description: A subscription is degraded but keeps running: global_scope_degraded = a new live call was not attached because this server already follows its cap of live calls (sent once per subscription while the cap holds)

WebSocketTranscriptSegmentEvent.description: One live transcript segment. seq is strictly increasing per call but not contiguous; a partial carries the seq its final will get

start_ms.description: Offset from the start of the recording

WebSocketSpeakerNamesEvent.description: Provisional live speaker names (the newest snapshot; the final transcript's naming replaces them). A final's name = the assignment of its speaker_label whose seq range covers its seq

WebSocketCallLifecycleEvent.description: A phase of the call: call_started, call_ended, transcript_provisional, transcript_ready or rescheduled. transcript_ready and rescheduled end the subscription (an unsubscribed frame follows; after rescheduled, subscribe again with the same event_id)

live_transcript_available.description: call_ended only: the provisional live transcript is available (null = unknown)

WebSocketGapEvent.description: No final between after_seq and next_seq arrived within the reorder wait (a capture relaunch skips 1,000+ numbers with nothing lost, or finals were never published). A late final may still follow: order by seq

WebSocketUnsubscribedEvent.description: A subscription ended: on request, after transcript_ready / rescheduled, 2 h after call_ended without transcript_ready, when the call will produce nothing more (capture failed, no call, published), or 12 h after the scheduled start

reason.description: requested | transcript_ready | rescheduled | no_transcript (2 h after call_ended) | call_not_live (capture failed, no call, or published) | max_duration (12 h after the scheduled start)

WebSocketErrorEvent.description: A client frame was refused (unavailable = an unexpected server failure, retry shortly); the socket stays open

id.description: Delivery id (= X-Invinite-Delivery); dedupe on it

created_at.description: When the event happened; deliveries are NOT ordered — order by this and the event phase

A temporary HLS playlist URL of an earnings call's live audio (PRO). The stream is watermarked.

### Using the URL

- The URL works until `expires_at` (2 hours by default) and is minted fresh on every request: request a new one before it expires.

- Play it with hls.js, Safari or VLC. The playlist is an EVENT playlist, so seek to 0 for the start of the call.

- `call_t0` is the wall clock of call ms 0: `#EXT-X-PROGRAM-DATE-TIME` minus `call_t0` = the `start_ms` of the live transcript (WebSocket channel `live_channel`).

### No stream and errors

- `status` `not_started` / `disabled` answer `url: null`.

- `403 audio_unavailable` when the company's audio is not licensed for delivery.

- `503 media_unavailable` while live streaming is not configured.

### Choose the call

- By `event_id`, or

- by `identifier` with `year` + `quarter` (fiscal), or

- by `identifier` with `date` (a calendar day in New York time (America/New_York); a call without a confirmed time is listed on its announced date). With `date`, `event_type` (default `earnings_call`) also addresses an investor day, conference or shareholder meeting.

### Freshness and coverage

- Data is replicated from the capture pipeline with a lag of about a minute.

- Only US earnings calls captured by Invinite are served.

get.description:
Forward guidance or every reported KPI figure of one earnings call.

### What you get

- `kind=guidance`: one consolidated item per metric, period and basis, with verbatim citations.

- `kind=kpi`: every reported KPI figure.

- The list is empty until the call has been derived.

### How far to trust it

- Guidance items are cross-validated between the call and the press release; `cross_validated=false` items come from one source only.

- `confidence` is calibrated on large-cap spot checks, not a probability.

### Links to SEC filings

- `filing_link` points at the SEC filing that carries the same figure: the results 8-K's press release (`target=press_release`, matched on the text) or, once the 10-Q / 10-K is on EDGAR, its XBRL fact (`target=periodic_filing`, `concept`), which replaces the 8-K link.

- `match_kind=rounded` means the filing's value rounds to the figure as spoken.

### Paging

- A page can hold fewer than `limit` items while `next_url` is still set: items (and KPI mentions) that only a press release no longer served supports are dropped after paging.

- Follow `next_url` until it is null.

The recording of one earnings call as a signed download URL (PRO). Audio files are forensically watermarked per customer: every account gets its own copy.

- An account's first request for a call answers `202` `{ status: "preparing", retry_after_seconds }` with `Retry-After` while that copy is prepared (not billed). Repeat the request after it.

- `403 audio_unavailable` when the company's audio is not licensed for delivery or no recording exists (one answer for both).

- `503 audio_temporarily_unavailable` while audio cannot be prepared.

- `503 media_unavailable` while media signing is not configured.

- by `identifier` with `year` + `quarter` (fiscal), or

- by `identifier` with `date` (a calendar day in New York time (America/New_York); a call without a confirmed time is listed on its announced date). With `date`, `event_type` (default `earnings_call`) also addresses an investor day, conference or shareholder meeting.

### Freshness and coverage

- Data is replicated from the capture pipeline with a lag of about a minute.

- Only US earnings calls captured by Invinite are served.

ws.summary: WebSocket filings stream and live earnings-call transcripts
ws.description:
One WebSocket connection streams new SEC filings as they are published and follows earnings calls live. Authenticate with your API key. WebSocket sessions cost no credits (hence no `x-credits`).

### Filings

- New SEC filings arrive as `new_filing` frames. The connection needs the STANDARD plan.

### Follow an earnings call live

Live transcripts use the channel `earnings-calls.live`, which requires the PRO plan.

1. Send a `subscribe` frame with an `event_id` or a `cik`. You receive `subscribed`.

2. `transcript_segment` frames arrive while the call is spoken; `speaker_names` snapshots name the speakers.

3. Lifecycle frames tell you where the call is: `call_started`, `call_ended`, `transcript_provisional`, `transcript_ready`, `rescheduled`.

4. The subscription ends with `unsubscribed` (its `reason` says why) after `transcript_ready` or `rescheduled`, 2 h after `call_ended` (the call produces nothing more), or 12 h after the scheduled start.

### Missed segments and reconnects

- Final segments arrive in `seq` order. A `gap` frame reports a range that did not arrive within 1.5 s; a late final may still follow.

- After a reconnect, subscribe again with `since_seq` set to the last final `seq` you hold: the missed finals are replayed, then live delivery continues. `resume_unavailable` means the call cannot be replayed.

- An `error` frame with code `unavailable` reports a server-side failure. The connection always stays open.

### Keyword alerts

- Add `keywords` (up to 20) to a subscription and every final segment that contains one also sends a `keyword_hit` frame. `keyword_match` is `exact` or `stem`; `speaker_roles` keeps, for example, management's words only.

- A hit carries the speaker's provisional name and role, the previous final segment as context, and `latency_ms`: the relay time inside the API process minus the segment's own end time (your network is not included).

### Guidance flashes

- Every subscription to a call receives `guidance_flash` frames: forward-looking numbers, extracted seconds after they are spoken.

### All live calls in one subscription

- `scope: all_live` with `keywords` (and no `event_id` or `cik`) follows every call being captured live for one subscription slot. It receives keyword hits only, never segments. `min_rank` limits the companies; `events` can add `guidance_flash`.

- A `warning` frame (`global_scope_degraded`) says a new call was not attached.

- At `transcript_ready` it also receives the final transcript's hits once (`layer: final`), without those a live hit already covered within ± 5 s.

### Live prices

- `prices: true` on a per-call subscription adds `price_tick` frames (at most one per second): that second's OHLC and volume, the return in bp since the last trade before the call started and since the previous close, and `call_ms` on the transcript clock.

- A tick shows what happened at the same time, not what caused it. Pre-market and after-hours bars are sparse.

- `prices` with `scope: all_live` is refused (`bad_message`). `GET /v1/earnings-calls/live` says `live_prices: true` while ticks flow.

Minimum tier for display: FREE.
